newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada insurers may face A.M. Best downgrade.
newsitem.headline: Canada insurers may face A.M. Best downgrade.

text.p: U.S. insurance ratings agency A.M. Best Co said on Friday that the Canadian life and health insurance industry is so competitive that downgrades of some companies are likely.

The Oldwick, New Jersey-based ratings agency said consolidation of the Canadian insurance industry has accelerated, putting increased pressure on Canadian insurers to increase their operational efficiency.
"Companies that lack a core strength -- be it a secure product niche or distribution system -- are likely to see their ratings lowered," Best said in a statement.
The ratings agency said even companies with superior ratings "cannot rest on past laurels."
"They will have to continue to distinguish themselves in a saturated life and health market and demonstrate that their advantages are sustainable," Best said.
It said value added products geared to retirement savings, individual, group life and disability insurance will be the key to long-term viability for Canadian insurers.
